title: Japan E-2D Static Frequency Converter
description: The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Lakehurst intends to negotiate and make an award on a sole-source basis with Aviation Ground Equipment Corporation, CAGE: 0TZM0 for a Fixed-Price contract. This procurement is for a quantity one (1) Converter, Frequency Static, part number 1000AG1000-2, for the Japan Air Self-Defense Force (JASDF). The JASDF requires the Converter, Frequency Static to take electrical power that comes in at one frequency and converts it to the exact frequency and voltage required by the aircraft's system The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 6.302-1, 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) �Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements� for this action. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. However, the Government will consider all responses received within fifteen days after the date of publication of this synopsis. Registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://www.sam.gov) is mandatory for consideration. A determination by the Government not to open the requirement to competition based on the responses to this notice will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for an award of a contract.

title: W50S8126QA014
description: PROJECT TITLE: REPLACE BLDG 33 ROOFPROJECT LOCATION: BARNES AIR NATIONAL GUARD BASETHIS PROJECT REQUIRES ALL LABOR, TOOLS, EQUIPMENT, MATERIALS, APPLIANCES, TRANSPORTATION, DOCUMENTATION, QUALITY CONTROL, AND SUPERVISION TO REPLACE THE POL OPERATIONS ROOF ON BUILDING 33, PROJECT NUMBER AXQD262336, AT 104 FW, BARNES ANGB, WESTFIELD, MA 01085. SCOPE: COMPLETE REMOVAL AND LEGAL DISPOSAL OF APPROXIMATELY 1600 SF OF EXISTING ROOFING MEMBRANE, 1200 SF OF INSULATION, AND FLASHINGS DOWN TO BARE STRUCTURAL ROOF DECK; DECK INSPECTION AND PREPARATION; INSTALLATION OF SELF-ADHERED BITUMINOUS VAPOR RETARDER; POLYISO RIGID AND TAPERED INSULATION ACHIEVING MINIMUM R-30 IN A MINIMUM OF TWO STAGGERED LAYERS; 1/2 INCH HIGH-DENSITY GLASS-MAT GYPSUM COVER BOARD; AND A FULLY ADHERED 90-MIL WHITE EPDM ROOFING SYSTEM. WORK ALSO INCLUDES 0.040 INCH PRE-FINISHED ALUMINUM FLASHINGS, EDGE METAL, AND TERMINATION BARS; REUSE AND REFLASHING OF ONE HVAC CURB, ONE EXHAUST FAN CURB, AND TWO VENT PIPES; 400 SF OF WALKWAY PADS; SEALING ALL PENETRATIONS; POLYURETHANE SEALANTS; FLOOD TESTING; ASTM C1153 INFRARED MOISTURE TESTING; ASTM E907 UPLIFT TESTING; DELIVERY OF A 20-YEAR NDL MANUFACTURER WARRANTY; A 5-YEAR CONTRACTOR WORKMANSHIP WARRANTY; AND CLOSEOUT DOCUMENTS INCLUDING INTERIM DD FORM 1354 AND O AND M DATA. WORK COMPLETED IAW STATEMENT OF WORK AND SPECIFICATIONS. 100 PERCENT SMALL BUSINESS SET-ASIDE: IAW FAR 52.219-6, QUOTES SOLICITED ONLY FROM SMALL BUSINESSES. QUOTERS MUST BE REGISTERED IN SAM.GOV AND MEET SIZE STANDARD. NAICS CODE 238160 (SIZE STANDARD $19.0M) AND PSC Z2JZ APPLY. MAGNITUDE OF CONSTRUCTION IS BETWEEN $50,000 AND $100,000. A SINGLE-AWARD FIRM-FIXED-PRICE CONTRACT IS CONTEMPLATED. SOLICITATION ISSUED AS AN RFQ UNDER FAR PART 13 AND FAR PART 36. AWARD WILL BE MADE ON INITIAL QUOTES WITHOUT NEGOTIATIONS TO THE RESPONSIBLE QUOTER SUBMITTING THE LOWEST EVALUATED PRICE CONFORMING TO ALL REQUIREMENTS. SOLICITATION, NOTICES, AND AMENDMENTS POSTED AT HTTPS://PIEE.EB.MIL AND SAM.GOV.

title: Repair collision damage to 2023 Dodge Durango Pursuit
description: This requirement is for repairing body damage and to perform necessary mechanical repairs on a 2023 Dodge Durango Pursuit (Tag number G62-6665Z, VIN# 1C4RDJFG3PC573974). The damage is due to Traffic Accident. Description of work includes Repair of all body damage to the vehicle body, frame, lights and structural components. The requirement is to repair this unit completely for return to service. All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer's warranty. All items shall include standard warranty. Repairs will be completed in accordance with industry standards. Vendors shall be in compliance with all EPA and OSHA standards and requirements. MSDS and any other required documents must be on site. Vendors must be properly insured to cover any losses for GSA vehicles that are in their shop. Valid business license(s) is required in accordance with state and local guidelines. All employees of the selected vendor must be paid in accordance with local Department of Labor established wages.

title: 513 CVN MCS Seaport
description: --- The procurement is limited to SeaPort-NxG (Multiple Award Contract (MAC) holders only. This solicitation will be competed under the SeaPort-NxG MAC amongst all MAC holders on an unrestricted basis. --- The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD), Code 513, requires contractual support for the provisioning of modernization-engineering, life cycle, and in-service engineering support to meet readiness and safety criteria. The support shall include computer program development, systems engineering, testing, equipment harvesting, integrated logistic support (ILS), waterfront support and installation for new ship construction and in service ships for CVN68 Class, CVN78 Class, Columbia Class, FF(X) Class, Amphibious ships, USCG cutters, and FMS vessels and other new ship classes. This support is applicable for Machinery Control Systems (MCS), Damage Control Systems, and Network Systems. The resulting award will be a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) SeaPort-NxG Task Order.

title: Radiographic Testing (RT) of a large aluminum weldment
description: SOURCES SOUGHT/REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR Radiographic Testing (RT) of a large aluminum weldment for Letterkenny Army Depot (LEAD) The Army Contracting Command, Redstone Arsenal � Letterkenny Army Depot (ACC-RSA-LEAD) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) and Source Sought announcement to gain information from industry and seek sources capable of and interested in providing radiographic testing (RT) of a large aluminum weldment, approximately 14x11x4 FT and thickness of weld joints 1.5-2.0� (more in some locations). All services will be expected to be performed at LEAD. Service provider will be expected to travel to LEAD within 24 hours notice to perform RT operations. Requirements could range in service timeline required and could be subject to daily needs or perhaps months-long gaps in service. Requirements will be expected to meet list of standards provided. Servicer will be responsible for bringing all required equipment for operation from taking images to evaluating them on-site. Methodology whether film, computer, or digital is permitted and subject to contractor discretion and shot requirements. There will often be real-time need for results with asset production and welding being on-hold until RT is completed. Current production outlook is 18 cabs / units in total. 3 cabs will require 100% RT in compliance with print 12940852 E Redline to include all ~230 shots per cab, even those struck out by the redlines. The other 15 cabs will require RT in compliance with 12940852 E Redline as it is written, ~ 37 shots required per cab. There are provisions in the 12940852 print for sampling plans and rework outcomes which would require additional shots to be taken on failed cab and those that follow. The overall project is expected to span late 2026 through 2031. The purpose of providing this information is to conduct Market Research and identify interested sources capable of inspecting these items. The following prints and standards apply to this requirement: 12472301 12553209 12940852 E Redline ASTM E1742 ASTM E1032 Mil Std 1895B Mil Std 2035A Mil Std 3057 Mil Std 370A The drawings for this requirement is export controlled, Distribution D, which contains unclassified sensitive military data. Only vendors who have a current DD Form 2345 � Military Critical Technical Data Agreement on file with Defense Logistics Information Service (DLIS), recent and acceptable NIST rating and Current DoW contracts are authorized to receive the drawing. Interested vendor(s) may request a copy of the applicable drawing via e-mail. Please contact Mr. Thomas Hall at Thomas.c.hall111.civ@army.mil. Contractors must be properly registered in the Government System for Award Management database (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220, or via the Internet at www.sam.gov. Eligibility At this point, the Government requests the response from all interested capable businesses and the applicable NAICS for this requirement is 541380 � Testing Laboratories and Services with a small business size standard of $19 Million. At this time, the Government has made no decisions about whether a full and open competition will occur. Upon receipt of all responses to this notice, the Government will determine its path forward. Capabilities Statement and additional Information and Submission Details REQUESTED INFORMATION: Please provide a Capabilities Statement, which must address the following items: Company Information: Please provide your Company Name, CAGE Code, UEI Number, and physical address of your primary facility. Socioeconomic Status: Based on NAICS Code 541380 (Testing Laboratories and Services), what is your business size? Please list all applicable socioeconomic categories (e.g., Small Business, WOSB, SDVOSB, HUBZone, 8(a)). System for Award Management: Is your company currently registered and active in SAM.gov? Manufacturer vs. Distributor: For this specific requirement, will your company be the Manufacturer of the radiographic testing, or will you be acting as a distributor/dealer supplying the end-item of another manufacturer? Corporate Experience & Capability 5. Company Experience: Describe your company's experience over the last five years in performing radiographic testing (RT) on large aluminum weldments, particularly for military or aerospace applications. Please provide at least two examples of similar projects, including the scope, duration, and customer. 6. On-Site Operations: Detail your experience in setting up and conducting RT operations at a client's facility, specifically at a government or military installation like an Army Depot. 7. Turnaround Time: The requirement states a need for real-time results as asset production will be on hold. Describe your standard process for providing on-site image evaluation and delivering immediate results to production personnel. What is your typical turnaround time from image capture to providing a pass/fail determination? Personnel Qualifications 8. Certifications: Confirm that all personnel who will perform and interpret radiographic tests are certified in accordance with MIL-STD-3057, ASNT CP-189, or NAS410. Please specify which certification(s) your personnel hold and their certification levels (e.g., NDT Level II, Level III). 9. Inspector Experience: Provide details on the qualifications and years of experience of the NDT Level II or Level III inspectors who would be assigned to this project. Specifically, detail their experience with interpreting radiographs of aluminum welds according to military standards like MIL-STD-2035A and MIL-STD-1895. Technical Approach & Equipment 10. RT Methodology: The requirement permits film, computed, or digital radiography. Which method(s) does your company specialize in? Describe the advantages of your proposed methodology for this specific application (large aluminum structure, variable shot requirements). 11. Equipment: Provide a comprehensive list of the equipment you would bring on-site to perform all required tasks, from image capture to on-site evaluation. Include details on the radiation source (X-ray/Gamma-ray), imaging plates/film, processing/scanning equipment, and viewing/evaluation software and hardware. 12. Standards Compliance: Confirm your capability and standard procedures for performing RT in accordance with the following standards: MIL-STD-3057 (Arc Welding of Armor Grade Aluminum) MIL-STD-1895 (Radiographic Procedures for Partial-Penetration Aluminum Welds) MIL-STD-2035A (Nondestructive Testing Acceptance Criteria) ASTM E1742 (Standard Practice for Radiographic Examination) ASTM E1032 (Standard Practice for Radiographic Examination of Weldments Using Film) 13. Shot Execution Plan: Describe your approach to performing the high volume of shots required (approximately 230 shots for the first 3 cabs and 37 for the remaining 15), including how you would manage location marking, setup efficiency, and ensuring full coverage as per print 12940852. Operational & Logistical Capability 14. Rapid Deployment: The government requires service providers to be on-site at Letterkenny Army Depot (LEAD) within 24 hours of notification. Describe your logistical plan to meet this rapid deployment requirement, including personnel and equipment mobilization. 15. Scheduling Flexibility: This project involves an inconsistent workload, with potential for daily needs followed by months-long gaps in service between 2026 and 2031. How would your company manage personnel and resource allocation to accommodate this unpredictable schedule while ensuring availability? 16. Safety Plan: Provide an overview of your company's Radiation Protection Program (RPP) and safety procedures for conducting RT operations on an active production floor, ensuring the safety of both your personnel and nearby government employees. title: CentralSquare Pro Cloud Software and Services
description: NASA�s Information Technology Procurement Office (ITPO) has a requirement for CentralSquare Pro Cloud software and services to support mission?critical Computer?Aided Dispatch (CAD) and Records Management System (RMS) operations for NASA Protective Services. The requirement includes cloud?based CAD dispatch positions, mobile CAD licenses, field operations modules, GIS mapping and AVL playback, GovCloud?hosted CAD and RMS environments, CLQ location services, SMS paging, API connectivity, and CrimeView analytics subscriptions for integrated crime?data analysis. Together, these components provide a unified, secure, AWS?hosted platform that enables real?time dispatching, mobile responder connectivity, NIBRS?compliant reporting, and data?driven situational awareness across all NASA centers. NASA/ITPO intends to issue a sole source contract to acquire the services from CentralSquare Technologies, LLC of 1000 Business Center Drive, Lake Mary, Florida 32746-5585 under the authority of FAR 6.103-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. CentralSquare Technologies, LLC is the sole source provider for this requirement. The Government intends to acquire a commercial product or service using FAR Part 12. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort electronically via email to caitlin.m.poulton@nasa.gov and sara.stuart@nasa.gov not later than 1:00 PM ET on September 29, 2026. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct this acquisition on a competitive basis. A decision by the Government not to compete this acquisition on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. title: USFS R6 Consolidated Snowmobile and ATV Purchase
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. Quotes are being requested. The U.S. Forest Service, Region 6, has a requirement for the procurement and delivery of one (1) All-Terrain Vehicle (ATV) and four (4) snowmobiles. All vehicles must be delivered new, fully assembled, fluids serviced, and in a 100% turnkey state ready for immediate field deployment upon arrival to support field operations in the Pacific Northwest (PNW) National Forests. Schedule of Items & Delivery Locations All shipments shall be shipped FOB Destination and contract line item pricing must be fully inclusive of all freight, handling, and delivery charges. CLIN 0001: All-Terrain Vehicle (ATV) Quantity: 1 EA Delivery Location: Hood River Ranger Station, 6780 Hwy 35, Parkdale, OR 97041 CLIN 0002: Snowmobiles (#6120, #6121) Quantity: 2 EA Delivery Location: Deschutes National Forest, Scott Street Compound, 80 SE Miller Ave, Bend, OR 97702 CLIN 0003: Snowmobiles (#6678, #6680) Quantity: 2 EA Delivery Location: Siuslaw National Forest, 1850 NE Four Acre Place, Corvallis, OR 97330 Key Technical Salient Characteristics (see attached salient characteristics for additional specs) General (All CLINs): Brand new only; manufactured in the U.S.; minimum 1-year manufacturer warranty; one operators manual per vehicle. CLIN 0001 (ATV): 4-stroke liquid-cooled gasoline engine (600cc�800cc); automatic CVT transmission with H/L/N/R; selectable 2WD/AWD/4WD; single passenger; min 4.0-gallon fuel tank; weight under 800 lbs; wheelbase under 55 inches; integrated cargo racks; 1.25-inch rear receiver hitch. CLIN 0002 (Snowmobiles): 550cc�650cc liquid-cooled engine; Mandatory factory-installed spark arrestor; minimum 2-person seating; heavy-duty rear utility cargo rack kit compatible with 154-inch track footprint. CLIN 0003 (Snowmobiles): 800cc�850cc 2-stroke liquid-cooled engine (91+ octane premium fuel); Mandatory factory-installed spark arrestor; 1-person seating; minimum 146-inch track length; integrated rear bumper tow package/hitch; dual electric and pull start; grip warmers. Award Structure & Evaluation The Government intends to evaluate quotes using simplified commercial procedures and may make up to two (2) separate Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) awards to achieve the most advantageous solution. Vendors may bid via three options: Option A: CLIN 0001 only (ATV) Option B: CLINs 0002 and 0003 only (Snowmobiles�must price both) Option C: All line items (CLINs 0001 through 0003) Quotes will be evaluated via side-by-side Comparative Evaluation based on the following criteria: Technical Capability & Salient Characteristics Delivery Timeline: Must be delivered within 90 calendar days from the date of award (shorter timelines may be evaluated more favorably). Price: Evaluated for fairness and reasonableness. Submission Instructions Quotation packages must be submitted via email to MINDY HICKMAN at mindy.hickman@usda.gov. Closing Date: Offers must be received no later than September 29, 2026, at 11:00 AM PDT. To be considered for award, the package must contain: SF-1449: Completed and signed (Blocks 17a, 30a, 30b, and 30c). Your Unique Entity ID (UEI) must be included in Block 17a. SF-30 Amendments: Acknowledged and signed copy of any posted amendments. Schedule of Items: Completed pricing using the provided Government form. Technical Documentation: Submit spec sheets, or product brochures for the offered Snowmobiles and ATVs to verify technical acceptability.

The purpose of this project is to construct 24 concrete turning pads, along with required site drainage improvements and road alignment and repair as necessary. title: INVITATION TO SUBMIT AN EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI) - Office Space
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is asking interested parties to provide information for a potential lease of space that meets the following criteria: Section A: Lease Components • a lease term of approximately 10 years, commencing on or about December 1, 2029, with a right of early termination anytime on or after December 1, 2037 provided written notice is given at least 12 months prior; • approximately 983 usable square metres (um2) of contiguous office space; • approximately 50 um2 of contiguous storage space; basement storage space is preferred; • the proposed space must be available approximately 48 weeks prior to the above-noted lease commencement date so all space(s) may be prepared for occupancy; • the proposed space should satisfy or be capable of satisfying the following criteria: 1. must be within office or commercial type buildings; buildings situated within heavy or medium industrial zoning and industrial type buildings with warehouse or manufacturing space will not be considered. A mixed use building may be considered at the sole discretion of PSPC; 2. proposed space must be contiguous and located entirely on one floor; 3. the dimensions must be compatible for efficient design and use; 4. a minimum floor loading capacity of 10.0 kPa (208.9 lbs. per square foot) for 70 um2 of the above-noted office space requirement; 5. a dedicated telecommunication/equipment room measuring no less than 9.0 um² within the proposed space must be provided; this area will not form part of the Lessee’s usable area noted above but will be included in the rentable area calculation; 6. daytime cleaning must be available; 7. access to a loading area must be available; 8. be fully accessible to persons with a disability; 9. a public transit stop must be within 600 metres of the buildings main entrance, and the frequency of service must not be greater than 30 minute intervals between the hours of 0700 hours and 1800 hours, Monday to Friday inclusive and there must be an accessible walking route between the public transit stop and the building; 10. acceptable space for the installation of a bicycle rack(s); 11. the physical characteristics of the Lands and the Building and the area and environment surrounding it, including neighbouring land uses, shall be compatible with the Lessee’s intended use of the accommodation; • the proposed space must be located in the City of Saskatoon. • on or before the lease commencement date, the proposed space will have to comply with all requirements contained in PSPC’s Standards for Leased Accommodation, a copy of which may be obtained from the contact listed in Section F; Note: PSPC may wish to visit or inspect the proposed space upon reasonable notice and a threat and risk assessment may be undertaken in order to assess potential threats to the security of the proposed space and to the public.

title: USCGA T-Boat Dry Dock Services.
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. The USCG is currently in the process of determining the acquisition strategy for this acquisition. To that end, the USCG is seeking to identify potential Contractors that possess the capabilities to provide Dry Docking Services for Training Boats (T-Boats) at the USCG Academy. Anticipated NAICS Code for this requirement: 336611 - Ship Building and Repairing Anticipated PSC Code for this requirement: J020 (Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment) This is a sources sought notice and request for information (RFI). The Draft Specification is attached for reference to a list of work items and specific work item details, as well as the drydock T-Boat size and weight. No cost or pricing data is required in the vendor�s response to this sources sought notice. Place of Performance: The T-Boats to be serviced are located at the USCG Academy in New London, CT. There is a 100 nautical mile geo-restriction for dry docking services for these T-Boats. Period of Performance: The USCG expects to award this contract with the base year in FY27. There are approximately four (4) T-Boats in need of dry-dock servicing and repairs. It is anticipated that two (2) T-Boats will be dry-docked in FY27, and another two (2) T-Boats will be dry-docking in FY28. The Government anticipates the first T-Boat dry-docking to start in early March 2027. Following completion of the first T-Boat dry-docking, options may be exercised for the subsequent T-Boats to be dry-docked in sequence. The Government may only allow one T-Boat to be dry-docked at a time. The anticipated Request for Proposal (RFP) release date for this effort is on or around 30 October 2026. Planned availability and RFP dates are subject to change. Any interested party may submit a capability statement by 4:00pm ET by Tuesday, September 29, 2026. The capability statement shall address your organization's ability to perform (inclusive of sub-contracting for elements) all of the work functions required per the attached Draft Specification. When submitting a capability statement, please include the following information: Company name; Company address; Company Point of Contact (POC) information; Company�s Unique Entity ID and CAGE number; Company�s socio-economic status(es)/business size status � including for the applicable NAICS; Does your facility have a dry-dock that can accommodate the T-Boat? If yes, which one and where is it located?; Does your company have availability to perform this dry-dock within the performance periods noted in this sources sought?; How much time would your company need from date of award to the start of the dry-dock?; Whether your company has certified welders or is able to sub-contract certified welders for process type(s); Whether your company has the mechanical ability and experience to: remove/install propellers, prop shafts, rudders, shaft and rudder bearings, valves, strainers, windlass servicing, engine to prop shaft alignment and various other mechanical systems; Whether your company has the ability to: perform pressure testing of various voids, valves, strainers, etc.; perform electrical generator servicing and repairs; perform lead abatement procedures; complete industrial paint removal processes and marine coating systems applications, as well as complete required coating system testing and inspections; and conduct weld inspections. Whether your company has the ability and experience to crop, align, and renew propeller shaft stern tubes; and Any vendor feedback/input or recommendation to the USCG on the Draft Specifications or any other aspects of this effort. RFI responses shall be limited to a total of twenty (20) pages. Respondents shall not submit any proprietary information when responding to this RFI. Respondents shall also note that the Government will not return any information submitted in response to this RFI. This is not a formal solicitation. Any formal solicitation will be announced separately at a later time. Information provided to the Government as a result of this posting is strictly voluntary and given with no expectation of compensation, and clearly provided at no cost to the Government. Information received in response to this sources sought will be used for market research purposes only. Questions, comments, or capability statement(s) in response to this RFI should be directed to the Contract Specialist, Romeo Rigor, at Romeo.M.Rigor@uscg.mil, with the Contracting Officer, Alan Boucher, at Alan.C.Boucher@uscg.mil cc:ed. Correspondence shall be via e-mail only (no phone calls/voice mail messages regarding questions/comments/capability statement(s) will be accepted nor will they receive a response). Please indicate in the subject of your e-mail: RFI Submission � USCGA T-Boat Dry Dock Services.

title: SOLE SOURCE � Procurement of Neuron, Linear Accelerator (LINAC) and Combined Environmental Testing Services
description: A solicitation will NOT be posted to https://www.sam.gov due to the sole source nature of this requirement. ITEM DESCRIPTION- Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC), Crane Division, has a requirement and intends to award an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for the procurement of Neutron, Linear Accelerator (LINAC), and Combined Environment Testing Services in support of the Radiation Combined Environment Test Capability (RCETC) and military hardware survivability validation programs. The proposed contract action is for the supplies and services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source: Amentum Services Inc., 4800 Westfields Blvd, Ste 400, Chantilly, VA 20151 (CAGE: 5W3V7) under the authority of FAR 6.103-1[JP1] , "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements" (10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1)). The basis for restricting competition is the lack of sufficient technical data, the extreme duplicative cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition, and the unacceptable, mission-critical delays in fulfilling the agency's requirements through any other source. To sustain reliable, technically advanced nuclear weapon effects (NWE) simulation testing without duplicating massive prior Government investments in pre-project planning, hosting solution design, and facility systemization, the Contractor must possess immediate, turn-key site and operational readiness. Specifically, the only source capable of satisfying this requirement must possess: Secured Real Estate: Existing secured real estate located within immediate proximity to NSWC Crane, Indiana, to support physical GFE delivery, secure handling, and immediate logistical integration. 100% Completed Facility Designs: Completed and Government-approved facility architectural/engineering (A/E) designs (including civil, structural, mechanical/electrical utilities, and verified radiation shielding calculations) optimized to house the Government-Furnished Property (GFP). Advanced Regulatory & Safety Bases: Completed and mature Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) license applications, Indiana Department of Health (IDoH) device registrations, Hazard and Operability Studies (HAZOP), and finalized Safety Basis/Radiological Control program documentation tailored explicitly to the safe operation of the high-intensity simulator sources. Established GFE Vendor Integration: Matured coordination, transition planning, and technical exchanges with the GFE manufacturer (Verus Research) to support immediate systemization, Operational Site Acceptance Testing (OSAT), and long-term capability sustainment. The contractor will be responsible for the end-to-end operation, availability, maintenance, and enhancement of NSWC-owned NWE simulators (specifically the Dense Plasma Focus (DPF) and Electron Linear Accelerator (LINAC) systems), associated diagnostics, and other GFP. No other source possesses the requisite specialized facility infrastructure, site readiness, and technical safety/regulatory baseline to perform these efforts immediately upon award. Any attempt to re-initiate the facility design, licensing, and systemization processes with another vendor would result in an unacceptable delay of multiple years and a substantial, non-recoverable duplication of cost to the Government. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement or proposal which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of re-evaluating the justification for sole source or limitation of sources and making a determination to change the acquisition strategy to a competitive procurement. The Solicitation and amendments for this sole source action will not be posted to sam.gov and are available only from the POC identified below. Request for Proposal (RFP) will not be made available through https://www.sam.gov. The RFP will be provided to directly to Amentum through electronic mail. The proposed noncompetitive contract action is anticipated to be awarded under FAR Part 15, Contracting by Negotiations. Contractors must be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://www.sam.gov. Questions or inquiries should be directed to Jamie Wilson, Code: 0233, Jamie.k.wilson1.civ@us.navy.mil. Please reference the above solicitation number when responding to this notice.

description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 1240BE26Q0103 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for a contractor to provide HVAC Controllers Service & Maintenance at El Portal & Catalina. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 811310. The small business size standard is $12.5 million. Submission of Quotes All quotes must be submitted via email to Contracting Officer, Andrea (Annie) Pollock at andrea.pollock@usda.gov. Quotes submitted through any other method will not be accepted or considered. Quotes are due at 4:30 p.m. ET on September 28,2026. Statement of Requirement The U.S. Forest Service at El Yunque National Forest (EYNF) requires services to maintain building HVAC Controllers in safe, reliable and efficient operating condition & routine maintenance services. Pricing includes all costs associated with providing HVAC Controller maintenance services in accordance with manufacturer�s warranty including materials, labor, overhead and profit. The contract will be for a base year, with four one-year optional periods of performance in accordance with the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS).

title: Image Intensifier (I2) Tubes ENVG PSQ-20B
description: In accordance with RFO FAR 5.1, this is a pre-solicitation notice ("synopsis") that DLA Weapons Support at Aberdeen anticipates issuance of a Request for Proposal (RFP) on or about 28 September 2026, for the following item listed below to support the AN/PSQ-20B Enhanced Night Vision Goggle. The NAICS code is 334511. The Government possesses a limited technical data package (TDP) for the part. The TDP is available for conditional release per distribution statement. The TDP includes conceptual information. This is not for a developmental effort. Alternate designs must be approved by the Government. This is not a solicitation. This is only an estimate and will not bind the contractor or the Government in any way or at any time into a contract with any of the specified terms below. The proposed contract type is a commercial, five (5) year, Firm-Fixed Price (FFP), Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (ID/IQ) with a maximum contract value of $9,809,553.85. NSN 5855-01-738-9480 Image Intensifier Tube P/N OFM-2307-A2 Annual Best Estimate Quantity (BEQ) = 400ea � 625ea. Note: The annual BEQ of 400ea � 625ea per year is listed for planning purposes only. Actual annual ordered quantities may be more or less than the annual BEQ. Image Intensifier Tube (I2 Tube) to support the AN/PSQ-20B Enhanced Night Vision Goggle and their associated technical data, are restricted from export by the International Trafficking in Arms Regulation (ITAR), Part 121, Category XII. The TDP is subject to the Internal Traffic in Arms Regulations. Any Offeror who wants to request a copy of the TDP must be registered in the Joint Certification Program, website is below: https://public.logisticsinformationservice.dla.mil/PublicHome/jcp/default.aspx Requests for a copy of the TDP after the RFQ is issued must include proof of DD Form 2345 JCP Certification and proof of Facility Security Clearance (FCL) / Level of Safeguarding for Classified Information / Material of SECRET / SECRET. The anticipated hardware ship to location will be W25G1U, New Cumberland, PA. The Government required delivery will be listed in the solicitation. A DD 254 Contract Security Classification Specification is part of this requirement and will be included in the RFP. -------------------------------------------------------- Please do not wait until the last minute to submit your proposals. To avoid potential submission of a late proposal, we recommend the transmission of your proposal file 24 hours prior to the required proposal due date and time. Contracting Office Address: Place of Performance: 6565 Surveillance Loop, RM C4 126B Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland 21005-1846 United States Primary Point of Contact: Pricilla Coppedge Pricilla.Coppedge@dla.mil

title: Preparation and Preservation in Potable Water Tank Onboard Submarine
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for a modified commercial service acquisition prepared in accordance with simplified acquisition procedures found in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Revolutionary Far Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 12.2, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation whereby quotations are being requested. This solicitation is intended to result in the issuance of a singular firm fixed price award. Solicitation Number N62789-26-Q-3001 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular FAC 2026-01 dated March 13, 2026. This is an unrestricted acquisition using NAICS Code: 336611, size standard: 1,300. This work is performed onboard a submarine located at a pier at the Naval Submarine Base New London. The intended period of performance is October 30, 2026�November 30, 2026. Offerors should recognize the preparation and preservation work is not consecutive in schedule and requires the offeror to complete the preparation and then come back to the Naval Submarine Base New London to complete the preservation. The successful offeror is required to work 7 days per week 2 shifts per day until task completion; and is also required to demonstrate it is able to support an on-site response within a 2-hour notification in order to support a highly sensitive ship schedule. The successful offeror is required to provide the Government with documentation of each of the following qualifications (or NAVSEA approved alternatives with proper documentation): AMPP C7, AMPP C12, AMPP C14, AMPP CAS LEVEL 2 and QP-1. The successful offeror is also required to be at least �LEVEL 1; SELF� Certified in the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) within the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) module in the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE). This requirement is found in DFARS Provision 252.204-7025 and Clause 252.204-7021 as both are contained in the solicitation. Please provide a quote along with three recent contracts exemplifying recent and relevant past performance. The quote shall also state the total price of the work and further broken down by Contract Line Item Number (CLIN). Please include as much detail as possible to assist in an expeditious evaluation. CLIN 0001: Preparation Efforts. Prepare Potable Water Tank #2 in accordance with the included statement of work. Contractor to clearly state the number of people performing work, hours per person, job title of each person and corresponding labor rate, total number of days required to complete the preparation. Vendor shall consider this requirement calls for the vendor to complete the preparation by working two shifts, seven days per week, inclusive of holidays, as necessary. CLIN 0002: Preservation Efforts. Preserve Potable Water Tank #2 in accordance with the included statement of work. Contractor to clearly state the number of people performing work, hours per person, job title of each person and corresponding labor rate, total number of days required to complete the preservation. Vendor shall consider this requirement calls for the vendor to complete the preservation by working two shifts, seven days per week, inclusive of holidays, as necessary. CLIN 0003: Material Costs. Contractor to state material costs to be incurred in support of the tank preparation and preservation. Contractor to break down or clearly state the materials to be consumed (consumables, paint, fuel, rentals, disposal etc.). CLIN 0004: Contractor Travel/Per Diem. Contractor to state travel costs to Naval Submarine Base New London for two (2) occurrences for the tank preparation and preservation efforts. Contractor to provide a complete breakdown of travel plans (number of people travelling, hotel costs, flights, car rental expenses, meals/incidentals) to assist in evaluation. The anticipated award will be made to the responsible vendor that can satisfy this requirement in conformance with the solicitation and is determined to be the best value to the government, price and other factors considered. In determining the best overall response, the combined non-cost/price factors (technical qualification and past performance) are more important than the cost/price factor. The Government may select for award the offeror whose price is not necessarily the lowest, but whose technical quotation is more advantageous to the Government and warrants the additional cost. The evaluation factors considered for this award are listed below and also contained in Section M of the solicitation. Offers that take exception to any performance criteria are unacceptable. Quotations are due prior to 5:00 P.M., EST on September 29, 2026. Late submissions will not be accepted. Offers should be submitted via electronic mail to: andrea.a.cook.civ@us.navy.mil and stephanie.l.neale.civ@us.navy.mil. Offerors should identify the RFQ number in the subject line of the email. Offerors are advised to submit electronic documents early and to confirm successful transmittal. The System for Award Management (SAM) is a Government maintained database of companies wanting to do business with the Government. A firm must register and maintain an active SAM registration in order to receive a federal award. Register at: https://sam.gov/SAM/pages/public/index.jsf EVALUATION FACTORS FOR AWARD: Technical Qualification Past Performance Price

The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), on behalf of Strike Weapons Program Office (PMX-201), is seeking to determine industry�s capabilities to design, develop, test, and fabricate cost-effective, rapid prototyping alternatives for the of the Silent Anvil Air-Launched Torpedo (SAA-LT). SAA-LT is a next-generation Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) standoff delivery system being developed by the U.S. Navy to address emerging threats in undersea warfare. It is designed to expand the range of manned and unmanned aircraft platforms capable of executing ASW missions. SAA-LT will be captive-carried and released from both internal and external aircraft weapons stations utilizing standard Department of War (DOW) carriage systems. SAA-LT will operate as a precise and highly maneuverable glide weapon, transitioning quietly to target areas to engage enemy submarines from distance. Prototyping Objectives & Timeline Demonstration: Demonstrate an end-to-end prototype capability of the SAA-LT system within eighteen (18) months of agreement award Fabrication: Rapidly assemble and deliver approximately one hundred eighty (180) prototype all-up-rounds (AURs) within the three (3) years following the successful end�to-end demonstration. Acquisition Pathways The Navy is exploring two parallel design options and invites industry partners to respond to Option 1, Option 2, or both: Design Option 1 (End-to-End Solution): A complete, integrated SAA-LT solution from aircraft separation to the underwater target. Design Option 2 (Wing Kit Standoff Design): An unpropelled glide wing kit configured to carry a Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) / Government Furnished Information (GFI) effector (torpedo) to the target area. The Government is considering utilizing the Naval Air Systems Consortium (NASC) to potentially award one or more OTAs pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 4022 �Authority of the Department of Defense to carry out certain prototype projects�. Note: If an interested person is a foreign concern or if a U.S. interested person has a team member or partner who is a foreign entity, adherence to all International Traffic and Arms Regulations (ITAR) is required. If space offered is above the ground floor, a minimum of two accessible elevators must serve the proposed floor. One of the accessible elevators may be a freight elevator. In cases where multiple spaces are offered within the same building, the Government reserves the right to select the space(s) that will be acceptable and reject the others. Lessor shall test for radon using EPA-approved methods and certify the results to the GSA Contracting Officer upon award. Co-tenants within the building shall be professional office environments. Buildings with windows comprising 50 percent of the exterior perimeter wall are preferred. Class A buildings preferred. Offered space must meet Government requirements for fire safety, accessibility, seismic, and sustainability standards per the terms of the Lease. A fully serviced lease is required. Offered space shall not be in the 1-percent-annual chance floodplain (formerly referred to as �100-year� floodplain). title: Market Survey for the procurement of NSN 6150-01-455-4207/PN A3354293, 6150-01-486-6937/PN A3357168 (LOAD BANK, ELECTRICAL) for Patriot MS EPP III
description: The Defense Logistics Agency-Aberdeen, on behalf of the Army Integrated Logistics Supply Center (ILSC) � Supply Chain Management Directorate (SCMD) � Strategic Sourcing Directorate (SSD), intends to acquire Parts to support the Electric Power Plant (EPP III) on the PATRIOT Missile Defense System. Requirements Description: The load bank is a piece of electrical test equipment used to simulate an electrical load, to test an electric power source. The load bank is used to provide field preventive maintenance checks and services of the Electric Power Plant (EPP III) on the PATRIOT Missile Defense System. The EPP III is the main electric power source for the PATRIOT Missile Defense System. The load bank is used on the 150 KW, 400Hz generator sets on the EPP III. Please note that this is not a Request for Proposal. This notice is provided for planning purposes and is not to be construed as a commitment by the U.S. Government. The Government does not possess the technical data package (TDP) for the parts. The TDP is not available for release. The TDP includes level 3. production information. Notice, Response Due Date, and Points of Contact: This is NOT a Request for Quote or Proposal. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on this SSA or reimburse any costs associated with the preparation of responses to this SSA. This Sources sought announcement (SSA) is for planning and market research purposes only and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government. title: M82 and M82A1 Percussion Primers
description: The Army Contracting Command - Rock Island is issuing Request for Proposal, W519TC-25-R-0016, to the SAM.GOV website with a closing date of 31 August 2026. title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Studie Zukunftsprojektion und Entwicklungspotentiale der Kultur- und Kreativwirtschaft 2037
description: In den vergangenen fast 20 Jahren seit Gründung der Initiative Kultur- und Kreativwirtschaft (KKW) der Bundesregierung haben sich die Rahmenbedingungen, Marktstrukturen, Wertschöpfungsketten und Herausforderungen für die KKW grundlegend verändert. Kaum eine Branche ist von den Auswirkungen durch den Wandel von Transformation, Plattformökonomie, Digitalisierung und Künstliche Intelligenz so stark betroffen wie die KKW mit Auswirkungen u.a. auf kreative Produktion, Distribution und Rechteverwertung. Die kommenden Jahre werden durch weitere tiefgreifende technologische, wirtschaftliche und gesellschaftliche Umbrüche geprägt sein. Digitalisierung (insb. Künstliche Intelligenz), Nachhaltigkeit und neue Formen der Publikumseinbindung sind zu den zentralen Treibern der Veränderung geworden. Nach fast 20 Jahren ist es daher an der Zeit einerseits Bilanz zu ziehen, und andererseits den Blick nach vorne zu richten und Grundlagen für strategische Handlungsoptionen zu schaffen. Um den weiteren Strategieprozess evidenzbasiert führen zu können soll eine qualitative und quantitative Grundlagenstudie zur Zukunftsprojektion für die KKW in Auftrag gegeben werden. Die letzte Grundlagenstudie „Gesamtwirtschaftliche Perspektiven der Kultur und Kreativwirtschaft“, ebenfalls erstellt im Auftrag des BMWE, stammt aus dem Jahr 2009. Die Studie soll eine Projektion für die kommende Dekade entwickeln, um strategische Antworten auf strukturelle Veränderungen der Branche zu geben. Es geht darum, die Zukunftsfähigkeit der KKW kritisch zu beleuchten, Risiken zu identifizieren sowie eine Prognose zu Chancen und Trends zu entwickeln. Die Studie „Kultur und Kreativwirtschaft 2037“ (Arbeitstitel) soll mit Hilfe zukunftsorientierter und prognostizierter Szenario-Analysen ein Fundament für eine langfristige strategische Ausrichtung politischer und ökonomischer Steuerungsinstrumente liefern. Für eine Zukunftsprojektion bis 2037 ist daher entscheidend, nicht allein bestehende Wachstumsverläufe fortzuschreiben, sondern strukturelle Brüche, neue Wertschöpfungslogiken und disruptive technologische Entwicklungen systematisch in die Prognose einzubeziehen. Als Grundlagen sind hier die Projektionen der Bundesregierung zum gesamtwirtschaftlichen Wachstum angemessen zu berücksichtigen. Die Studie soll ein wissenschaftliches Fundament für die strategische Weiterentwicklung der Initiative Kultur- und Kreativwirtschaft der Bundesregierung schaffen und dabei insbesondere eine langfristige strategische Ausrichtung politischer und ökonomischer Steuerungsinstrumente liefern. Die Strategie richtet sich perspektivisch an Entscheidungsträgerinnen und -träger aus Politik, Wirtschaft, Verwaltung sowie an die Akteure der Kultur und Kreativwirtschaft selbst, die gemeinsam die Weichen für ein nachhaltiges, innovatives und wirtschaftlich starkes Kreativökosystem der nächsten Generation stellen wollen.

title: Denmark – Business services: law, marketing, consulting, recruitment, printing and security – Udbud af rammeaftale vedrørende levering af pædagogiske vikarer til Hillerød Kommune
description: Udbuddet omfatter levering af pædagogiske vikarer til daginstitutioner i Hillerød Kommune. Ydelserne omfatter alene vikartimer afholdt i dagtimer på hverdage inden for følgende kategorier af vikarer:PædagogerPædagogmedhjælperePædagogiske assistenterAftalen er rettet mod Ordregivers daginstitutioner, der har et behov for vikarer. Ordregiver kan og vil indgå aftaler om levering af pædagogiske vikarer rettet mod andre typer af behov og afdelinger, som fx vikarer til botilbud og andre særtilbud.Aftalen omfatter er rettet mod levering af vikarer, når Ordregivers eget vikarkorps samt Ordregivers faste pædagoger, pædagogmedhjælpere mv. ikke kan dække behovet. Krav til vikarerne samt vilkår for bestilling og levering fremgår af Aftalen med tilhørende bilag - herunder særligt Bilag 1 – Kravspecifikation.Der arbejdes med to overordnede typer af vikarbestillinger: Akutvikarer og Planlagte Vikarer.Aftalen giver ikke vindende tilbudsgiver krav på eller garanti for et bestemt antal timer/vagter. Leverancernes omfang bestemmes alene af de bestillinger, som de enkelte Bestillere hos Ordregiver løbende afgiver. Forbruget er således bestemt af det faktiske behov for i Ordregivers afdelinger og institutioner, og Ordregiver er ikke forpligtet til at aftage et vist minimum.Der er i Aftalen krav om en minimumsleveringsgrad, hvorved menes, hvor stor en procentdel af alle bestillinger som den vindende tilbudsgiver skal dække.Kravene er en leveringsgrad på 92 % for Akutvikarer og 95 % for Planlagte vikarer. Såfremt de fastsatte leveringsgrader ikke overholdes, vil der være tale om mislighold der blandt andet vil kunne medføre et krav om betaling af en bod.

title: Belgium – Environmental services – European Monitoring of Biodiversity in Agricultural Landscapes (EMBAL) 2028
description: OBJECTIVES: The general objectives of this contract are to contribute towards i) the establishment of a robust data series on the state of biodiversity in agricultural landscapes in the EU, and ii) a better understanding of (the impacts of policy actions on) the biodiversity trends in agricultural landscapes at the EU and national level. The specific objectives of this contract are i) to undertake the EMBAL field survey in all EU Member States in 2028 and 2029, and ii) to analyse the collected data. The contract will survey at least 4500 sites in each year (i.e. undertake at least 9 000 site-surveys across the two years), strictly following the EMBAL survey protocol and technical guidelines as prepared and executed in the EMBAL survey 2022/2023. TASKS: 1) Preparation of the field survey (including sampling strategy and design, pre-processing of monitoring sites, selection and recruitment of surveyors, material and equipment, digitised data workflow, helpdesk, quality control and contingency planning); 2) Execution of the field survey; 3) Data post-processing; 4) Data analysis; 5) Organisation of a conference to present the results. title: Germany – Installation of partitioning – Kurparkterrassen Bad Neuenahr-Ahrweiler / Büro- und Veranstaltungsgebäude: Glastrennwandsystem / Aluminium-Glastrennwandsystem
description: Der Kurpark Bad Neuenahr ist eine denkmalgeschützte Parkanlage, welche Bestandteil der baulichen Gesamtanlage Kurbezirk ist. Mit dem Thermalbadhaus, dem Steigenberger Kurhotel sowie dem Kurhaussaal mit Spielbank bildet der Kurpark das historische Kurviertel des Stadtteils Bad-Neuenahr. Im südlichen Randbereich des Kurparks befindet sich das Gebäude Kurparkterrassen. Es handelt sich um ein zweigeschossiges Gebäude mit Untergeschoss. In massiver Bauweise 1972 errichtet, wurde das Gebäude durch die Flutkatastrophe im Juli 2021 im Unter- und Erdgeschoss stark beschädigt. Im Erdgeschoss wurde ein Wasserstand von 1,78 über Oberkante Fußboden gemessen. Das Erdgeschoss wurde vor der Flutkatastrophe als Bürofläche der Ahrtal Marketing GmbH (AMG) sowie als temporäre Veranstaltungsfläche ("Kleine Bühne") als Kompensation für die bereits rückgebaute, gegenüberliegende Konzerthalle genutzt. Die Nutzung entsprach einem städtischen Verwaltungs- und Veranstaltungsgebäude (Bürgerhaus). Das Obergeschoss wurde für Besprechungen, Kurse und Lagerflächen genutzt. Im Untergeschoss waren Lager- und Gesellschaftsräume verortet. Weiterhin wurde aufgrund der Flut das damals bestehende Technikgebäude des Großen Sprudels zerstört. Die Brunnentechnik wurde daraufhin temporäre in den Außenbereich verlegt und soll nun in das Untergeschoss des Gebäudes Kurparkterrassen integriert werden. Um den neuen und gewachsenen Flächenanforderungen der AMG Sorge zu tragen wurde innerhalb des ersten Planungsprozesses eine mögliche Sanierung mit potentieller Erweiterung untersucht. Aufgrund der gegebenen technischen Sanierbarkeit des Gebäudes, wurde im weiteren Zuge der Vorentwurfsplanung ein kostentechnischer Vergleich von Sanierung und Neubau erstellt. Als Ergebnis wurde festgestellt, dass die Sanierung und Erweiterung des Gebäudes nicht nur unter wirtschaftlichen, sondern auch unter dem Aspekt der Nachhaltigkeit die besser Lösung darstellt - CO2 Einsparung, die Nutzung bereits gebauter Kubatur sowie der Erhalt des architektonischen Gesamtkonzeptes. Das Gebäude Kurparkterrassen bildet mit dem Neubau der Kurparkliegenschaften ein Gesamtensemble. Gestalterisch lehnt sich das Gebäude Kurparkterrassen an den Neubau der Kurparkliegenschaften an. Dieses Ensemble wird über die Wiederherstellung der ehemaligen Kolonnade (Wandelgang) zwischen dem Neubau der Kurparkliegenschaften sowie dem Gebäude Kurparkterrassen vervollständigt.

title: Germany – Architectural, engineering and planning services – BG Klinikum Hamburg - Neubau Bergedorf - Allianzpartner 2 - ARCH | Integrierte Gebäude-, Freianlagen- und Verkehrsplanung
description: Gegenstand des Projektes ist der Neubau des Berufsgenossenschaftlichen Klinikums am Standort Hamburg-Bergedorf. Dieses soll auf seinem bestehenden Areal mit einer Größe von rund 25,3 ha grundlegend neu organisiert und zu einem zukunftsweisenden Klinikcampus mit rund 350 Betten entwickelt werden. Die Zielgrößen für den Neubau umfassen eine Bruttogrundfläche (BGF) von ca. 66.000 qm und eine Nutzungsfläche (NUF) von ca. 30.000 qm. Darüber hinaus ist im Rahmen des 2. Bauabschnitts eine Erweiterung des Reha-Angebots um ca. 11.000 qm vorgesehen. Zusätzlich sind Erweiterungsflächen von ca. 10.000 qm zu berücksichtigen. Damit ergibt sich eine Gesamtnutzungsfläche von ca. 51.000 qm. Ziel der Planung ist die Schaffung eines modernen Gesundheitsstandorts, der ambulante und stationäre Versorgung in einem funktional und räumlich integrierten Neubau vereint und moderne Infrastrukturen sowie optimale Arbeitsbedingungen für eine hochspezialisierte medizinische Versorgung schafft. Im Mittelpunkt steht eine Spitzenmedizin mit Rehabilitationsauftrag aus einer Hand, die konsequent auf den langfristigen Behandlungserfolg ausgerichtet ist. Der Klinikcampus bildet das vielfältige medizinische Leistungsspektrum des Standorts ab. Er umfasst insbesondere die Bereiche Diagnostik und Therapie für die stationäre und ambulante Versorgung sowie weitere Funktions- und Nutzungsbereiche, unter anderem für Forschung und Lehre, Erschließung, Ver- und Entsorgung, sonstige Einrichtungen (u. a. MVZ und Versorgungstechnik) sowie die Freianlagen. Weiterführende Angaben zu den Flächenquantitäten sowie zum Raumprogramm und zu den funktionalen und räumlichen Affinitäten innerhalb des Raumprogramms (Betriebsorganisationsplanung) werden mit der Aufforderung zur Angebotsabgabe zur Verfügung gestellt. Die Planung soll eine wirtschaftliche, flexible und zukunftsfähige Krankenhausstruktur schaffen, die modernste medizinische Versorgung mit den Prinzipien der Healing Architecture verbindet. Mit dem Neubau soll ein landschaftsbezogener Klinikcampus entstehen, der eine heilungsfördernde Umgebung für Patientinnen und Patienten sowie attraktive Arbeitsbedingungen für Mitarbeitende schafft.

title: Germany – Facade work – Geschwister-Scholl-Gymnasium Erweiterungsbau - Fassade GU
description: Die Stadt Garbsen plant die Erweiterung des Geschwister-Scholl-Gymnasiums mittels Anbau auf der ehemaligen Sportplatzfläche des TSV Berenbostel, welche sich nördlich des Bestandsgebäudes des Geschwister-Scholl-Gymnasiums befindet. Der geplante Erweiterungsneubau lehnt sich an die städtebauliche Vorgabe des bestehenden Gymnasiums an und ergänzt das Ensemble mit einem dritten, leicht aus der Orthogonalität heraus geschwenkten Riegel. Dadurch wird ein neuer Pausenbereich aufgespannt der in Form eines "shared space" durch die Außenanlagen gestaltet wird. Der dreigeschossige Neubau hat eine Abmessung von ca. 85 m x 32 m und ist längs nach Ost-West ausgerichtet. Der Haupteingang liegt quer zum Riegel und ist über einen markanten Unterschnitt des Erdgeschosses im Südwesten klar zu erkennen. Ein durchgestecktes Eingangsfoyer führt in eine dreigeschossige Halle mit Bühne und Sitzstufen, das "Herzstück des Neubaus". Von dort aus lässt sich das Organisationsprinzip des Dreibunds leicht erkennen. Im äußeren Bund befinden sich die Hauptnutzungsbereiche, wie Verwaltung, Klassenräume, Fachklassen etc. und im Inneren zwei Belichtungshöfe, eine Technikzentrale und weitere Nebenräume, die als Kerne ausgebildet sind. Die erforderlichen fünf Lerncluster sind jeweils an den Stirnseiten des Riegels angeordnet. U-förmig rahmen sie eine innere Mitte, die den fünf bzw. sechs allgemeinen Unterrichtsräumen pro Cluster vorbehalten sind. Je zwei eingeschnittene Terrassen und Loggien in den Ober-geschossen brechen die Cluster auf und lassen einen direkten Außenbezug zu. Die Anordnung von Klassenräumen um ein zentrales Forum ermöglicht eine zukunftsorientierte Pädagogik, die auf eine Vielzahl von flexiblen Nutzungsmöglichkeiten reagieren kann. Zwei tief eingeschnittene Innenhöfe sorgen für Tageslicht und gliedern den Baukörper in drei Abschnitte: Cluster - Gemeinschaft - Cluster. Die Mittelzone des langgestreckten Baukörpers ist den gemeinschaftlichen Funktionen der Schule, wie Bibliothek, Musik, Kunst- und Werkräumen vorbehalten. Dort liegt auch die Haupterschließung, die über eine große Sitzstufentreppe und einer einläufigen Freitreppe bis ins 2. Obergeschoss führt. Darüber sorgt ein großes Zenit-Licht für ausreichend Tageslicht. Auf den Zwischenpodesten entstehen Kommunikations- und Ausstellungsflächen, die gemeinschaftlich genutzt werden können. Im obersten Geschoss bietet sich die Option, den Luftraum mit einem Netz zu überspannen und mit einer weiteren Lese- und Chill-out-fläche für einen Perspektivwechsel bei Schüler*innen zu Sorgen. Kaskadenartige Terrassen zum westlichen Innenhof schaffen ebenfalls den unmittelbaren Außenbezug im Inneren. An der Nordseite stellen zwei weitere Treppenhäuser die notwendigen baulichen Flucht- und Rettungswege sicher. Das Gebäude wird in der Bauweise eines Holzhybrid-Skelettbaus ausgebildet. Das bedeutet, dass vornehmlich Stahlverbundstützen an den Fassaden und Holzstützen im Innenraum den Lastabtrag übernehmen, wodurch eine größere Grundrissflexibilität erreicht wird. In Teilbereichen übernehmen Stahlbetonkerne die Aussteifung des Gebäudes. Auf der Gebäudelänge ist eine Brandwand nach 60 m über alle Geschosse mit einzuziehen. Die Bodensohle ist aus Stahlbeton, Decken und Dachkonstruktionen werden aus Stahlbetondecken in den Kernen und an den Innenhöfen sowie Holzhybridelementen erstellt, die über holzverkleidete Stahlverbundträgern abgetragen werden. Im Zuge dieser Maßnahme werden Fassadenarbeiten ausgeschrieben.

title: Germany – Business services: law, marketing, consulting, recruitment, printing and security – 10020615-Framework agreement for expertise on green hydrogen and battery value chains in South Africa
description: The project "PtX & Battery Value Chains in South Africa - Expert Pool (H2.SA II / BVC)" supports the development of a sustainable green hydrogen, Power-to-X (PtX) and battery economy in South Africa. Implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, the project is part of H2.SA II / BVC, which is co-funded by the European Union and runs until 2030. South Africa has significant potential to develop competitive green hydrogen and PtX industries due to its renewable energy resources, existing infrastructure, industrial base and potential domestic and international markets. At the same time, the country has significant potential to develop sustainable battery value chains, building on its established automotive industry and access to critical raw materials. The project provides support to public and private stakeholders to create an enabling policy and regulatory environment, strengthen capacities, improve the bankability of projects and develop sustainable and inclusive value chains. Its areas of work include strategy, policy and regulatory frameworks; private sector cooperation and finance; capacity strengthening, research and development; sustainability and just transition; and battery value chains. To respond flexibly and efficiently to the diverse and evolving demand for specialised expertise, GIZ intends to establish a framework agreement with an expert pool. The framework will enable the rapid mobilisation of qualified international and local experts for individual assignments addressing specific technical, economic, financial, environmental, social, regulatory, certification and battery value-chain related needs.

Assistance instruments or CFDA opportunities are anticipated and will be CALL dependent. PROPOSAL DUE DATE AND TIME: This BAA will remain open for a period of 10 years from the date of publication. NO PROPOSALS SHOULD BE SUBMITTED AGAINST THIS BASELINE BAA. Proposal due dates and times will be specified in each CALL. Proposals received after the due date and time specified in the CALL shall be governed by the provisions of FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). It should be noted that this installation observes strict security procedures to enter the facility. These security procedures are NOT considered an interruption of normal Government processes, and proposals received after the above stated date and time as a result of security delays will be considered "late". Note: If offerors use commercial carriers for delivery of proposals, carriers may not honor time-of-day delivery guarantees on military installations. Early proposal submission is encouraged. BRIEF PROGRAM SUMMARY: This is a 10 year BAA describing the research areas of interest for the Research Options for Space Enterprise Technologies (ROSET). This closed BAA approach allows for submittals at a specified date and time, which will be posted through the issuance of CALL announcements at various times against this BAA. This BAA will be reviewed no less frequently than annually and updates will be published in SAM.gov. Any changes or cancellation of the BAA will be posted as amendments to this BAA. The annual reviews and subsequent amendments to the BAA shall meet the requirement of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 35.016. As requirements within the technical topic areas are identified, CALLs will be issued in SAM.gov to request proposals for specific research efforts. These subsequent CALLs will contain specific descriptions of the research effort to be addressed, anticipated period of performance, information pertaining to the specific research technical topic area, and the estimated funding profile for the CALL. GENERAL INFORMATION: This acquisition will be UNRESTRICTED. Small businesses are encouraged to propose on all or any part of the BAA CALLs based on CALL specifics. This BAA is issued under the provisions of FAR 6.102(d)(2) that provides for the competitive selection of research proposals. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA that are selected for award are considered to be the results of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of Public Law 98-369, the Competition in Contracting Act of 1984. Offerors MUST monitor SAM.gov http://www.sam.gov in the event this announcement is amended and for the posting of CALLs. CALLs: A CALL is a required posting, issued through SAM.gov (http://www.sam.gov), soliciting a specific/targeted response and/or proposal for specific research efforts. A CALL will contain a specific description of the research effort to be addressed, the anticipated period of performance, and any other information particular to the specific requested effort. CALLs are published independently at various times during the open period of the BAA and may use either a One-Step or Two-Step process. A CALL issued against the BAA will specify either a direct request for a technical and cost/business proposal, or a white paper submission as a means to determine if proposal will be required. TYPE OF CONTRACTS/INSTRUMENTS: The Air Force reserves the right to award the instrument best suited to the nature of the research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) or Non-FAR instruments (i.e. Other Transaction (OT) for research efforts, grants, and cooperative agreements). For non-FAR Instruments, CALLS will be posted on grants.gov. The Government anticipates that a mix of contract types and other instruments will be used throughout the life of this BAA. Generally, awards under this BAA may be Cost plus Fixed Fee (Completion and Term), Cost Contract, Firm Fixed Price, Other Transaction Authority, Technology Investment Agreements, Grants, or Cooperative Agreements. Cost type contracts will require successful Offerors to have an accounting system deemed adequate by Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) for tracking costs under a cost reimbursable contract (DFARS 242.75). If an Offeror does NOT have a DCAA approved accounting system, a Cost plus Fixed Fee and Cost Contract cannot be awarded. ANTICIPATED NUMBER OF AWARDS: The Air Force anticipates awarding a minimum of one contract per specific CALL. However, the Air Force does reserve the right to make multiple awards or no awards pursuant to a CALL. description: MARKET SURVEY/CAPABILITY ASSESSMENT FOR NATIONAL TEST EQUIPMENT PROGRAM (NTEP) OFFICE (AJW-1610) BLANKET PURCHASE AGREEMENT (BPA) TO SUPPLY TEST EQUIPMENT (TE) REQUIRED TO SUPPORT THE NAS. The purpose of this announcement is to conduct a market survey to solicit statements of interest and capabilities from interested vendors in accordance with Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Acquisition Management System (AMS) Policy 3.2.1.2.1. This market survey will enable the FAA to review responses that are current and will assist with acquisition planning based on the current data obtained. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has a requirement for the acquisition of multiple items of test equipment using a blanket purchase agreement (BPA). title: Facility Readiness and Maintenance Execution (FRAME) Request for Proposal (RFP) - DRAFT
description: This Special Notice provides interested parties with information regarding the availability of the draft Request for Proposal (dRFP), review requirements, the tentative acquisition schedule, and the upcoming Industry Day and Site Visit. This notice is for planning purposes only and does not constitute an invitation for bids, request for proposals, or quotes, nor does it indicate that the Government will contract for the items described herein. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submitting feedback or attending the events outlined in this notice. The 30th Contracting Squadron (30 CONS/PKD) at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB), CA, is requesting industry feedback on the dRFP for the Facility Readiness and Maintenance Execution (FRAME) contract. FRAME is the follow-on acquisition to the current Launch Operations Support Contract (LOSC) (Contract #FA4610-23-D-0001, currently performed by Call Henry, Inc.). FRAME follow-on acquisition is 100% Small Business Set-Aside. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 561210 Facilities Support Services (small business size standard is $47M). Description of Services, Background, and Objective: FRAME is a non-personal services contract that provides maintenance, repair, modification, and modernization for?over 130?facilities, property, and equipment (P&E)?supporting?the nation�s space mission, defense, and test activities at VSFB and its associated geographically-separated locations. The scope of work involves facility infrastructure and systems (including water and gas mains, roads, generators, power distribution, HVAC, waste systems, and roofing) alongside the execution of distinct sustainment projects and?standby support for urgent repairs during select?launch operations to ensure maximum operational readiness. Additionally, the contract encompasses the inspection,?testing,?and certification of all Space Launch Delta 30 cranes and elevators. A key change under this follow-on acquisition is that the South Vandenberg Power Plant (SVPP) is no longer a requirement and will not be carried over from the legacy LOSC to the new FRAME contract. The primary objective of the FRAME contract is to ensure Real Property Installed Equipment (RPIE) and facilities are maintained and operationally ready for a variety of ballistic missile, space, guided weapon, and aircraft test and evaluation missions in support of Space Launch Delta 30 (SLD 30), 30th Civil Engineer Squadron (30 CES), 4th Launch Squadron (4 LS), 2nd Range Operations Squadron (2 ROPS), Missile Defense Agency (MDA), U. S. Space Forces - Space (S4S), 18th Space Defense Squadron (18 SDS), Sentinel, 30th Operations Support Squadron (30 OSS), 2nd Space Launch Squadron (2 SLS), the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO), and various other Range Users. Mission Essential Services: The FRAME contract contains some mission-essential requirements which require continued support during peacetime, national emergency, and/or wartime scenarios. Tentative Acquisition Schedule: dRFP Release: 8 Sep 26 Final RFP Issuance: 12 Nov 26 Proposals Due: 16 Jan 27 Anticipated Award: 18 Dec 27 Performance Start:?1 Apr 28 4. Industry Day and Site Visit Event Details Interested businesses are invited to register for the upcoming two-day event. Representatives will have the opportunity to attend a briefing detailing the contract structure, tour key range facilities, and participate in one-on-one sessions with the Government program team. Dates: September 22, 2026 (General Briefing & Tour) � September 23, 2026 (One-on-One Sessions) Location: Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB), CA Maximum Attendees: Limited to two (2) representatives per prospective company due to base logistical constraints. Registration and RSVP Deadlines: Attendee RSVP & Security Vetting Submission: No later than Friday, September 11, 2026, at 16:30 Pacific Time. Provide your full name and company. Late requests may not be processed. One-on-One Meeting Request: Companies interested in booking a one-on-one session with the program office must explicitly request it via email by Tuesday, September 15, 2026, at 16:30 Pacific Time. Slots are limited and will be scheduled on a first-come, first-served basis. Maps and a tentative agenda are attached to this announcement to assist registered attendees with navigation and scheduling. Base Access & Entry Requirements: All site visit attendees must report to the Vandenberg Visitor Control Center (VCC), located at 6 California Blvd (Santa Maria Gate) prior to entry (VCC hours: 0600-1800). Arrive Early: Attendees are strongly encouraged to arrive early to the Visitor Control Center to allow sufficient time for base entry processing and to avoid delays getting to the briefing. Identification for Non-CAC Holders: Attendees who do not possess a Common Access Card (CAC) must present a REAL ID-compliant credential or a valid U.S. Passport. If an attendee does not have a REAL ID or a Passport, they must bring and present a standard state-issued Driver's License or ID card, a Birth Certificate, and a physical Social Security Card to obtain a base visitor pass. Foreign Nationals will not be able to participate due to the time necessary to vet access. 5. Important Site Visit Disclaimers & Rules of Conduct: Change of Solicitation Terms: Please understand that nothing said during the Industry Day briefings, site tours, or one-on-one sessions by any Government representative changes the terms, conditions, specifications, or requirements of the solicitation. If a change to the solicitation is determined to be necessary based on what is discussed or observed, it will be formally issued as a written amendment via email. Photography and Video Restrictions: No photography or video recording is permitted on this installation at any time, unless specific, designated areas are explicitly pointed out and authorized by the hosting Facility Manager. 6. Submission of Questions & Comments (CRM) The Government is actively seeking industry feedback on the Draft PWS and planned acquisition strategy to ensure clear, high-performing requirements. To submit questions or comments concerning the acquisition and dRFP, prospective offerors must use the official Comment Resolution Matrix (CRM) Excel spreadsheet (which will be posted with the Draft RFP documents). Completed CRM spreadsheets must be returned to the Points of Contact listed below. The deadline for submitting dRFP and Industry Day comments is September 29, 2026, by 16:30 Pacific Time. 7. Primary Points of Contact For all RSVP submissions, one-on-one requests, CRM question submittals or administrative questions, please send correspondence via email to BOTH of the following representatives: Primary POC (Contracting Officer): Katherine Williams, 30 CONS/PKD Email: katherine.williams.9@spaceforce.mil Secondary POC (Contract Specialist): Sabrina Swain, 30 CONS/PKD Email: sabrina.swain.1@spaceforce.mil 9/8/2026: This office is updating this draft RFP to update and add additional attachments.
